value.body: Training coordinators run the logistics of employee learning: induction for new joiners, skill and compliance training, and leadership programmes. They work in HR or learning and development (L&D) teams in companies, BPOs and training firms. A day might involve scheduling sessions, coordinating trainers, sending reminders and compiling feedback.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA (HR), BA, or an MBA in HR

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Learning management system (LMS), Excel, video-meeting tools

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: L&D coordinator, training executive, HR associate (L&D)

items.label: M.B.A. enrolment (all specialisations)
items.note: HR is one of several MBA specialisations

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually enter as L&D or training coordinators in large companies, BPOs and IT services firms that run regular induction batches. Clear communication, presentation skills and comfort with spreadsheets matter more than a specific degree.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the early work is logistics rather than designing content.
Common next steps: L&D specialist, trainer, or instructional designer.
Training budgets are often cut first when business slows.
